Śramaṇa.fact: But the Samanaeans are elected, and consist of those who wish to possess divine knowledge. But the Samanaeans are not the offspring of one family, being, as we have said, collected from every nation of Indians.

Śramaṇa.subject: Ancient India
Śramaṇa.question: A _____, however, is not a subject of any government, nor does he contribute any thing together with others to government
Śramaṇa.fact: On entering the order All the Bramins originate from one stock; for all of them are derived from one father and one mother. A Bramin, however, is not a subject of any government, nor does he contribute any thing together with others to government.

Śramaṇa.subject: Ancient India
Śramaṇa.question: And such is the life of the _____
Śramaṇa.fact: Having likewise the superfluities of his body cut off, he receives a garment, and departs to the Samanaeans, but does not return either to his wife or children, if he happens to have any, nor does he pay any attention to them, or think that they at all pertain to him. And such is the life of the Samanaeans.

Śramaṇa.subject: Ancient India
Śramaṇa.question: And when they enter into their house, the sound of a bell being the signal of their entrance, those that are not _____ depart from it, and the Samanaeans begin immediately to pray
Śramaṇa.fact: And when they enter into their house, the sound of a bell being the signal of their entrance, those that are not Samanaeans depart from it, and the Samanaeans begin immediately to pray.

Śramaṇa.subject: Ancient India
Śramaṇa.question: On food and living habits And with respect to those that are philosophers, among these some dwell on mountains, and others about the river _____
Śramaṇa.fact: On food and living habits And with respect to those that are philosophers, among these some dwell on mountains, and others about the river Ganges. But those that reside near the Ganges, live also on autumnal fruits, which are produced in abundance about that river.

Śramaṇa.subject: Ancient India
Śramaṇa.question: They spend the day, and the greater part of the night, in hymns and prayers to the _____; each of them having a cottage to himself, and living, as much as possible, alone
Śramaṇa.fact: They spend the day, and the greater part of the night, in hymns and prayers to the Gods; each of them having a cottage to himself, and living, as much as possible, alone.

Śramaṇa.subject: Ancient India
Śramaṇa.question: For the _____ cannot endure to remain with others, nor to speak much; but when this happens to take place, they afterwards withdraw themselves, and do not speak for many days
Śramaṇa.fact: For the Bramins cannot endure to remain with others, nor to speak much; but when this happens to take place, they afterwards withdraw themselves, and do not speak for many days.

Ṛta.subject: Ancient India
Ṛta.question: What do you know about In the Vedic religion, Ṛta (/ɹ̩t̪ɐ/; Sanskrit ऋत ṛta "order, rhythm, rule; truth?
Ṛta.answer: the principle of natural order which regulates and coordinates the operation of the universe and everything within it. I
Ṛta.fact: In the Vedic religion, Ṛta (/ɹ̩t̪ɐ/; Sanskrit ऋत ṛta "order, rhythm, rule; truth; logos") is the principle of natural order which regulates and coordinates the operation of the universe and everything within it. In the hymns of the Vedas, Ṛta is described as that which is ultimately responsible for the proper functioning of the natural, moral and sacrificial orders.

Ṛta.subject: Ancient India
Ṛta.question: Similar concepts exist in many Indo-_____ cultures and the names can in addition be derived from an identical root word *h₂r-tós
Ṛta.fact: Similar concepts exist in many Indo-European cultures and the names can in addition be derived from an identical root word *h₂r-tós. This is why some scholars take the position that the concepts in the Indo-European daughter cultures have a common ancestor in the Proto-Indo-European culture.
